blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Using the slant side instead of the perpendicular height.
- Confusing circumference $2\pi r$ and area $\pi r^2$; using the diameter in place of the radius.
- Forgetting the straight sides when the perimeter of a sector is required: perimeter = arc + 2r.

blocks.title: Example 1: sector
blocks.statement: A sector of a circle of radius 12 cm has angle 150°. Find the arc length and the area (π from the calculator, 1 d.p.).

blocks.title: Example 2: composite shape
blocks.statement: A window is a 10 m by 6 m rectangle with a semicircle of diameter 6 m on one of the 6 m sides. Find its area.
steps: Semicircle: radius 3 m: ½ × π × 9 = 14.14 m².

lessons.title: Volume and surface area of solids
lessons.programRef: O Level Mathematics — Mensuration (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Calculate volumes and surface areas of prisms, cylinders, cones, pyramids and spheres.
Convert between cm³, m³ and litres.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Volumes
blocks.md: Prism: area of cross-section × length. Cylinder, cone, pyramid and sphere:
blocks.tex: V = \pi r^2 h \qquad V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h \qquad V = \frac{1}{3} A h \qquad V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3

blocks.title: Surface areas
blocks.md: Cylinder (closed), cone (slant height l, with base) and sphere:
blocks.tex: 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h \qquad \pi r l + \pi r^2 \qquad 4\pi r^2

blocks.title: Units
blocks.md: 1 m³ = 1 000 000 cm³ and 1 litre = 1 000 cm³, so 1 m³ = 1 000 litres. The slant height of a cone is found by Pythagoras: $l^2 = r^2 + h^2$.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Using the slant height in the volume formula (use the perpendicular height h).
- Forgetting the ⅓ for cones and pyramids.
- Converting units wrongly: 1 m³ is 1 000 litres, not 100.

blocks.title: Example 1: a cylinder
blocks.statement: A water tank in Bamenda is a cylinder of radius 0.5 m and height 2 m. Find its capacity in litres (to the nearest litre).

blocks.title: Example 2: a cone
blocks.statement: A cone has base radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. Find the slant height, the volume and the total surface area (1 d.p.).
steps: Curved area πrl = 15π; base π r² = 9π; total = 24π ≈ 75.4 cm².

exercises.prompt: A solid metal cylinder of radius 4 cm and height 10 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 2 cm, with no metal wasted. How many spheres are made?
exercises.explanation: Cylinder: 160π cm³. Sphere: 4/3 × π × 8 = 32π/3 cm³. 160π ÷ (32π/3) = 15 spheres.
